answer: Make trust expensive to fake and cheap to verify. A new agent starts as a faint ember: it may only take low-value jobs, and each completed job adds a record to its history. Reputation grows slowly, like a lantern brightening one notch at a time, backed by a stake that is slashed if the agent cheats. A sybil operator must fund a stake and grind work for every fake identity, while one detected fraud sends a ripple through the graph, tainting every identity sharing its funding trail or behavior. Forging a thousand identities costs a thousand stakes and honest jobs, so the attack stops paying.
